findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_recent_registrations" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Registrations newly added to Meridian in the last N days, optionally filtered by market, risk class or device type — the competitor-monitoring feed. Ordered by …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_recent_registrations, check_issue · Private data: get_registration, find_distributors, find_predicates, classify_device, get_recent_registrations, get_coverage, report_data_issue, check_issue, report_outcome · Public sink: get_registration_timeline.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_recent_registrations, check_issue · Private data: get_registration, find_distributors, find_predicates, classify_device, get_recent_registrations, get_coverage, report_data_issue, check_issue, report_outcome · Public sink: get_registration_timeline

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_distributors" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
